judged_text: The DB-fallback credential fetch requires `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` to be truthy, but core calendar credentials (e.g. google_calendar credentials created before the App Store migration, or credentials whose App row is absent) have no related App record, so the constructed credential stays undefined and the destination is silently skipped. Legacy/pre-App-Store credentials referenced by a destinationCalendar.credentialId cause that host's calendar event to be silently not created (no error surfaced), reproducing exactly the class of silent-skip bug this refactor was meant to fix; the same copy-pasted fallback in updateAllCalendarEvents (lines ~505-520) and the one in handleCancelBooking has the same dependency.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the DB fallback only constructs a `credential` when `credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug` (see the `findUnique({ include: { app: { select: { slug:true }}}})` block and the subsequent `if (credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug) { credential = { appName: credentialFromDB.app.slug, ... } }`). If the credential row exists but has no related `app` (or no `slug`), `credential` remains undefined and the code silently skips creating the event for that destination (`if (credential) { ... createdEvents.push(...) }` with no else/error). The same pattern is present in the calendar-reference update path in `updateAllCalendarEvents` (the loop over `calendarReference` with identical `app?.slug` gating). This is a verifiable behavior from the diff and can cause destination calendars referenced by `credentialId` to be skipped without surfacing an error.
